title: Choose Inputs and Outputs
goals: Turn the project outcome into precise input and output requirements
Apply a simple manual baseline to valid requests and record its results
Plan a fair comparison using the same catalogue, requests and judging rules
vocabulary: A precise condition that the solution must satisfy
A defined starting method used for comparison
Meeting all the stated conditions of the request
A stated way to choose when several options qualify
A check of whether a result satisfies a requirement

worked_example.title: Describe a baseline someone else can repeat

blocks.title: The manual checklist baseline
rows: Check minutes and Yes or No
Check time and quiet for each
blocks.caption: The baseline is a complete manual method. A prototype must be compared with this defined procedure, not an invented weak opponent.

blocks.text: Write the request at the top of a sheet. If it is invalid, record what needs clarification and stop. Otherwise mark each catalogue row as compatible or incompatible using both conditions. Circle the first compatible row in order, or write no match if every row fails. Record the output and its reason. This checklist is our baseline.

The baseline can be correct on all cases when applied carefully. A prototype that matches it has not demonstrated better compatibility. It may still be easier to use or faster to trace, but those are separate claims that need their own measures. Do not make the baseline skip a condition just to make the prototype look better.

guided_practice.title: Run the baseline on three requests
guided_practice.prompt: Using the catalogue, record the baseline output and reason for 10 minutes with quiet required, 8 minutes with quiet not required, and 7 minutes with quiet not required. Identify which no-match result is justified and why.
guided_practice.answer: 10 Yes gives B1: 10 fits exactly and it is quiet. 8 No gives B2: B1 is too long, B2 fits and non-quiet is permitted. 7 No gives no match: even the shortest activity requires 8 minutes. That no-match result is justified by the complete catalogue.

independent_case.title: Build a baseline for a different catalogue
independent_case.task: A paper room recommender uses R1 first, capacity 6, quiet Yes; then R2, capacity 10, quiet No. Valid requests give a whole group size from 1 to 12 and Quiet required Yes or No. A room fits when capacity is at least group size and the quiet condition is met; choose the first fitting room. Record outputs and reasons for 6 people Yes, 8 people No and 8 people Yes. Explain how a manual baseline can be compared fairly with a prototype. No real booking is allowed.
independent_case.answer: 6 Yes gives R1: equality fits and it is quiet. 8 No gives R2: R1 is too small and R2 meets capacity with quiet not required. 8 Yes gives no match: R1 is too small, R2 is not quiet. Use the same room catalogue, request set and requirements for both methods and keep all results. Compare suggestions only; do not make bookings.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

blocks.text: INPUT  minimal required information
PROCESS  candidate decision process
OUTPUT  specific promised result and uncertainty path
CORE IDEA  A useful design makes required information and promised result explicit.

UNDER THE HOOD  Interface contracts define inputs, outputs, types, allowed values, missing-data behavior, and guarantees. Good design avoids collecting data that cannot improve the promised result and avoids promising outcomes the process cannot support.
Draw a fresh example with all three stages:
A closer explanation

These four rows are the complete approved catalogue for the paper model. Treat their times as fixed task values, not measured guarantees about real pupils. All required materials are assumed available. The catalogue order B1, B2, B3, B4 is the tie rule; it is not a claim that B1 is everyone’s favourite.

For 10 minutes with quiet required, B1 fits because 10 is no more than 10 and B1 is quiet. B2 fails the quiet requirement. B3 and B4 take too long. For 8 minutes with quiet not required, B2 fits; B1 takes too long. A request for 7 minutes has no compatible activity in this catalogue, even when quiet is not required.

Check each condition. A fast activity can still fail the quiet requirement. A quiet activity can still take too long. Exact equality is allowed: an activity listed as 10 minutes fits 10 available minutes. A blank time is different from a valid time of zero.
Connect the picture and the explanation
Point to the input, the deciding step and the result in this week’s visual. Explain the same step in ordinary words. A picture helps when you can say what each part represents.
